title: State of Rajasthan v. Biti K. Mohanty
crime_type: Foreign Tourist Rape / Jumped Parole / Identity Theft as Bank Officer
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / High Court of Rajasthan / High Court of Kerala
source: Supreme Court of India & Indian Kanoon
ipc_sections: Section 468 IPC (Forgery for purpose of cheating)
Section 471 IPC (Using forged document as genuine)
evidence: Conviction for raping German national in hotel room in Alwar based on prompt medical corroboration and victim statement
Disappearance while on 15-day parole granted to visit ailing mother in Odisha in November 2006
Fraudulent MBA degree, forged voter ID, and counterfeit PAN card obtained under alias Raghav Rajan
Fingerprint comparison by Kerala Police and National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) matching fugitive bank officer in Kannur
modus_operandi: After being convicted of raping a foreign national, suspect secured temporary parole through his father (a high-ranking DGP-level IPS officer) and absconded. Forged an entirely new identity as Raghav Rajan, secured a university degree, passed bank competitive exams, and worked as a branch manager at State Bank of Travancore in Kannur for seven years before fingerprint re-verification unmasked him.
personality_disorder: Chameleon-like sociopathic adaptation, persistent deceit, and exceptional ability to embed in professional institutions.
common_traits: Abusing judicial parole privileges to abscond
Total reinvention of identity with complete forged educational credentials
Securing professional white-collar banking employment under alias
Long-term evasion across distant linguistic states
summary: Spectacular fugitive capture case in Indian jurisprudence. The Supreme Court cancelled all lenient bail/parole indulgences, highlighting stringent requirements for identity verification of white-collar bank professionals.
